messages:
rachel: morning - saw a burst of fncall 'invalid_shape' events from payments-proxy. console shows red failures but the tool actually returned an array payload and the adapter could have coerced it. product confused.
dinesh: can you attach a sample?
rachel: sample from logs: validator_error: expected object, got array; sample='[{"order":"A1","qty":1}]'
maya: note: we enabled stricter fncall validation in a small canary last night. fallback routing to cheaper variant is on for rejects.
ollie: billing currently attributes charge to the execution model (final_model_id). observability increments validation_reject on origin route, which is why product sees failures on their route.
dinesh: proposal: console add a distinct "soft-fallback" state (amber) showing origin route + billed execution model + a redacted example; keep hard red for fatal rejects.
maya: telemetry: add tags fallback_reason, origin_route_id, execution_model_id, coercion_attempted. also add metric soft_fallback_rate with 5%/15m alert.
ollie: policy: introduce per-route setting `fncall_shape_policy` = strict|soft|coerce. default enterprise=soft. coerce means adapter may wrap array-> {items: array} before validation.
rachel: rollout tweak: exclude 'soft' and 'coerce' events from auto-flip calculations. auto-flip should only use fatal rejects or capacity fallbacks.
infra-bot: deploy 1797769000-fncall-validator-v3 -> succeeded (canary)
dinesh: action items: telemetry (dinesh), console UX (maya), validator codes + coercion hint (rachel), adapter opt-in coercion (ollie), alert rule (infra).
maya: I'll land console mock and a support playbook. if any route hits >10% soft-fallback pre-change, paste top 3 samples here and tag @eng-oncall. :eyes:
